indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of children aged 3 years to the starting age of compulsory education who participate in early childhood education programmes. It is expressed as a percentage of the population in the same age group. Data are collected from national administrative sources.
rationale: Early childhood education is key to preparing children for primary school and life-long learning. High participation rates reduce inequalities and support cognitive, emotional and social development from an early age. The long-term goal is to maximise participation of all children in quality early education.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national administrative sources and refer to children enrolled in ISCED 2011 level 0 (early childhood education) programmes. Coverage includes both public and private institutions. The reference population is children aged 3 years to the starting age of compulsory education.
